generated_by.method: web search + page reads; official sources preferred (service-public.gouv.fr, impots.gouv.fr, welcometofrance.com, france-visas.gouv.fr). Budget-capped session of 12 tool calls: 6 web searches and 6 page fetches. Of the fetches, one service-public.fr URL returned a 301 redirect to service-public.gouv.fr, one was a second read (later part) of the same service-public page, and one levels.fyi Paris URL had no data. Pages read in full: service-public F16922 (carte talent), impots.gouv.fr (impatriate regime), levels.fyi France. Other facts come from search-result snippets and are marked as such. Job boards were not probed this session; access notes are inference or carried over from the DE session (2026-11-22), as marked.

open_questions: EU Blue Card France: service-public says 3 years of experience within the last 7 is enough 'in listed professions'. Whether software engineers (ICT professionals) are on that list was not confirmed on an official page this session.

EU Blue Card France: whether a 3-year Indian BCA needs a formal comparability statement (France Education international / ENIC-NARIC France) or is accepted as is by the prefecture/consulate was not checked.

Decree n° 2026-1001 of 26 October 2026 (in force 30 October 2026) changes Blue Card validity, intra-EU mobility, job-loss rules and some prefecture processing times. Only search snippets were read; the exact new rules and any new decision deadlines should be read on legifrance.gouv.fr.

The EUR 39,582 reference salary comes from an arrêté of August 2025 (service-public cites 'Arrêté du 21 août 2025'; a secondary source says 29 August 2025). Whether a new arrêté changed it for 2026 or 2027 was not checked. The Blue Card figure EUR 59,373 = 1.5 x 39,582 (one secondary source links it to décret n° 2026-308).

Carte de séjour 'salarié' route: minimum salary, the employer tax amount (taxe employeur) and the current list of shortage occupations (métiers en tension, arrêté of 21 May 2025 per a service-public snippet) were not read. Whether software developer roles are on the Île-de-France shortage list is unknown.

Carte de résident (10 years): the exact eligibility for talent-card holders (5 years of residence) and for EU Blue Card holders (EU long-term resident status, possible aggregation of residence in other EU states) were not read on an official page. Language level B1 and the civic exam apply to a first carte de résident (service-public / justice.fr snippets); whether talent holders are exempt from either is not confirmed (a non-official blog was contradictory).
Whether the employer foreign-worker tax applies to the Blue Card (service-public states the exemption for the salarié qualifié card) was not confirmed.
Long-stay visa processing in India: france-visas gives a general 15 days (up to 45) decision time; no talent-specific or India-specific figure was found. VFS appointment wait times not checked.
2026 French income tax brackets and social-contribution rates were not researched this session.
Senior-specific salary band for Paris: levels.fyi shows only a Paris median (EUR 74,524) and France-wide percentiles; no senior-level split was visible.

Job-board access (robots.txt / ToS / APIs) for Welcome to the Jungle, France Travail, Indeed France and APEC was not checked. The France Travail job-offers API is known to exist via francetravail.io but its terms and key process were not read. Arbeitnow coverage of French listings not measured.
No official India-facing scam advisory for France (French embassy in India or Embassy of India in Paris) was read this session.

name: France

languages.note: English-only engineering roles exist in Paris, mostly at international tech companies, well-funded start-ups/scale-ups and foreign-owned firms, but French is the default working language at many local employers, consultancies (ESN) and in day-to-day admin. Expect many postings to ask for French. French at B1 is also required later for the 10-year carte de résident. Qualitative inference, not a measured statistic.

salary.note: Levels.fyi France, Software Engineer total compensation, all levels (1,082 data points, updated 2026-11-24): p25 EUR 47,258, median EUR 61,040, p75 EUR 77,549, p90 EUR 103,764. Paris median shown as EUR 74,524 (no Paris percentiles). low = Paris median, high = France-wide p90, used as a rough senior proxy; the Paris p90 is likely higher. Figures are total comp (incl. bonus/equity) and skew to large tech companies; base salaries at local firms and ESN consultancies are often lower. Note the EU Blue Card threshold (EUR 59,373 gross base) is below the Paris median total comp, but a base-only offer may not reach it.

income_tax_note: Progressive income tax plus substantial employee social contributions; 2026 brackets not researched this session. Impatriate regime (régime des impatriés, art. 155 B CGI, impots.gouv.fr, last modified 2026-04-08): for employees recruited directly from abroad (or moved within a group) who were not tax-domiciled in France in the 5 civil years before starting. The impatriation premium is exempt from income tax; if the contract does not set one, it can be taken as a flat 30% of remuneration. Runs until 31 December of the 8th civil year after taking up duties. Combined exemptions capped at 50% of total remuneration (or 20% cap on the foreign-activity part). Remaining taxable pay must be at least a reference pay for comparable roles. Not available to people who came to France on their own initiative.
cost_of_living_note: Paris rents are high and the rental market is competitive; landlords usually ask for a rental file (dossier) with French payslips, an employment contract and often a guarantor, which is hard for new arrivals, so temporary or corporate housing is common for the first months. Qualitative note, not verified with figures this session.

visa_routes.name: Talent – EU Blue Card (carte de séjour « talent – carte bleue européenne »)

salary_threshold.note: Gross annual salary of at least 1.5 x the reference average gross salary (EUR 39,582, set by an arrêté of August 2025) = EUR 59,373, per service-public.gouv.fr F16922 (checked 2026-06-01, read 2026-11-25). Gross, not net. Check for a newer arrêté before relying on it.

visa_routes.degree_requirement: Diploma from at least 3 years of higher education, OR 5 years of relevant professional experience; in listed professions, 3 years of experience gained in the 7 years before applying is enough. Employment contract of at least 6 months.
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: A 3-year BCA is a 3-year higher-education diploma, so on the face of the service-public text it meets the degree condition. Whether a comparability statement is required was not checked. A senior engineer with 7+ years of experience also meets the 5-years-of-experience alternative, independent of the degree.
visa_routes.processing_time: Long-stay visa: France-Visas says decisions usually take 15 days, up to 45 days in special cases (general figure, not talent- or India-specific); add VFS appointment time. Residence card: filed online on ANEF within 2 months of arrival when entering on a long-stay visa; prefecture silence after 90 days counts as implicit refusal (30 days if already holding another EU state's Blue Card). Decree 2026-1001 (in force 30 October 2026) changed some processing rules; not read.
visa_routes.path_to_pr: Card valid for the contract length up to 4 years (contract of 2+ years), or contract + 3 months up to 2 years. Renewable. A 10-year carte de résident can be sought later; for a first carte de résident, French at B1 and a civic exam (required since 1 January 2026) apply. Blue Card holders also have EU intra-mobility rights (move to another EU state after 12 months). Exact residence-duration rules for the carte de résident / EU long-term resident status not verified this session.
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: No work authorisation needed (service-public). Fees on the applicant side: long-stay visa EUR 99, then residence card EUR 350 (EUR 300 tax + EUR 50 stamp duty, paid by timbre fiscal); renewal EUR 250 per welcometofrance (qualified-employee page). Employers often reimburse these; not a legal rule. Whether the employer foreign-worker tax applies was not confirmed.

visa_routes.name: Talent – qualified employee, innovative-company track (« talent – salarié qualifié », parcours entreprise innovante)

salary_threshold.note: Gross annual salary of at least EUR 39,582 (reference average gross salary), per service-public F16922.

visa_routes.degree_requirement: No separate diploma condition listed on service-public. The employer must be a jeune entreprise innovante (JEI) or a company recognised as innovative by the Ministry of the Economy, and the job must be directly linked to the company's R&D project.
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: Not an obstacle: no diploma condition is listed for this track. The constraint is the employer type (JEI / recognised innovative company) and an R&D-linked role.
visa_routes.processing_time: Long-stay talent visa: usually 15 days, up to 45 (France-Visas general figure). Residence card via ANEF; prefecture silence after 4 months counts as implicit refusal for the salarié qualifié card.
visa_routes.path_to_pr: Card valid for the contract length, up to 4 years; renewable. First carte de résident (10 years) requires French B1 and the civic exam; exact residence-duration rules not verified this session.
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: No work authorisation needed. Applicant fees: visa EUR 99, card EUR 350 (EUR 300 + EUR 50 stamp). Service-public states the employer foreign-worker tax exemption for the salarié qualifié card; assumed to cover this track, not confirmed.

visa_routes.name: Talent – qualified employee, French-degree track (« talent – salarié qualifié », parcours salarié qualifié)

salary_threshold.note: Gross annual salary of at least EUR 39,582, per service-public F16922. Contract longer than 3 months.

visa_routes.degree_requirement: A diploma at least equivalent to a master's obtained in France, or a level-1 diploma labelled by the Conférence des grandes écoles from a nationally accredited institution.
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: Not eligible with a 3-year Indian bachelor's: this track needs a master's-level diploma obtained in France. Listed so the app can explain why the 'passeport talent' mentioned in postings may not fit; use the Blue Card or innovative-company track instead.
visa_routes.processing_time: Prefecture silence after 4 months counts as implicit refusal (service-public).
visa_routes.path_to_pr: Card valid for the contract length, up to 4 years; renewable. Carte de résident rules as above (B1 French, civic exam).
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: No work authorisation needed and the employer is exempt from the foreign-worker employment tax (service-public). Applicant fees EUR 99 visa + EUR 350 card.

visa_routes.name: Employee residence card with work authorisation (carte de séjour « salarié »)
visa_routes.degree_requirement: No specific degree rule found this session; the employer must obtain a work authorisation (autorisation de travail) through ANEF for each new contract.
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: Degree not the constraint on this route; the labour-market test and employer paperwork are. Fallback when the offer is below the Blue Card threshold and the employer is not a JEI.
visa_routes.processing_time: Work authorisation: prefecture silence after 2 months counts as implicit rejection (service-public F2728 snippet). Then the long-stay visa (usually 15 to 45 days). Overall slower and less certain than talent routes.
visa_routes.lottery_or_quota: No quota, but a labour-market test: the job must have been advertised with the public employment service (France Travail) for 3 consecutive weeks within the 6 months before the request with no suitable applicant, unless the occupation is on the shortage list (métiers en tension).
visa_routes.path_to_pr: Multi-year card after the first year, then carte de résident; first multi-year card and first carte de résident need the civic exam and French-language proof (levels per service-public F34501; not read in full). Not verified in detail this session.
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: Employer applies for the work authorisation and pays an employer tax for authorisations over 3 months (amount not researched). Heavy fines for employing someone without authorisation.

sponsor_register.how_to_use: France has no public register of employers approved to hire foreign workers; talent and Blue Card routes need no employer licence. The app cannot match employers against a register. Use posting text (sponsorship_phrases), company size/age signals and past hiring of international staff instead. A JEI (jeune entreprise innovante) status, relevant to the innovative-company talent track, is a tax status not published as an open list (not checked).

ease_for_indian_nationals.rationale: The EU Blue Card is reachable for senior engineers in Paris: EUR 59,373 gross threshold, no quota, no employer licence or work authorisation, and a 3-year bachelor's or 5 years of experience qualifies. The innovative-company talent track (EUR 39,582, no diploma condition) helps at JEI start-ups. Points lost for: the main 'passeport talent – salarié qualifié' track needs a French master's, so it does not fit a 3-year Indian degree; English-only jobs are a minority and French is needed for daily life and, at B1 plus a civic exam, for the 10-year card; prefecture/ANEF processing is slow and changed again in October 2026; base salaries at many local employers fall below the Blue Card threshold.

factors.degree_recognition: Blue Card: 3-year higher-education diploma or 5 years' experience (or 3 of last 7 years in listed professions). Salarié qualifié track needs a master's from France. Innovative-company track lists no diploma condition.
factors.language_barrier: Medium to high. English-only roles exist at international firms and start-ups in Paris; many employers, admin and housing require French. B1 French for the first carte de résident.
factors.processing_speed: Visa usually 15 days (up to 45). Residence card via ANEF afterwards; implicit refusal deadlines of 90 days (Blue Card) or 4 months (salarié qualifié) show that prefecture processing can be long.
factors.employer_willingness: No register to measure it. Large tech companies and funded start-ups in Paris do hire non-EU engineers on talent/Blue Card routes because no labour-market test applies; many local firms and ESN consultancies prefer candidates already authorised to work. Qualitative; no statistic gathered.
factors.attestation_or_paperwork: Degree and civil-status documents may need translation/apostille (see origins/in.json); comparability statement for the BCA not confirmed. Applicant pays visa EUR 99 and card EUR 350 unless the employer reimburses.

relocation_norms: International tech employers and scale-ups in Paris commonly cover visa/talent-passport filing through an immigration provider and offer a relocation budget or temporary housing; the impatriate tax regime is often applied for recruits from abroad. Smaller local firms and ESN consultancies offer less. Qualitative; not verified with survey data this session.

scam_warnings: App heuristic: talent-passport and Blue Card fees are paid to the French state (visa EUR 99 via France-Visas/VFS, card EUR 350 by timbre fiscal). Anyone asking the candidate to pay an 'agent', 'employer' or 'embassy contact' for a job, work permit or 'guaranteed visa' is high risk.

App heuristic: France has no sponsor register, so the app cannot confirm sponsorship from a register. Check the company in the French business registry (SIREN/SIRET) and that the posting domain matches the company's own site.

App heuristic: residence applications are made online on the official ANEF portal (administration-etrangers-en-france.interieur.gouv.fr) and visas on france-visas.gouv.fr; look-alike sites charging for 'assistance' or 'priority appointments' are a known pattern for visa services generally (not verified for France this session).
Other European missions in India (Norway, Denmark, Finland; see nl.json) warn of fake job offers and fake work permits; a job offer you never applied for and any fee charged for a job are red flags.
